source_text: Adiunxit plane et addidit legem certa nos condicione et sponaione constringens, ut sic nobis dimitti debita postulemus secundum quod et ipsi debitoribus nostris dimittimus, scientes inpetrari non posse quod pro peccatis petimus, nisi et ipsi circa peccatores nostros paria fecerimus. idcirco et alio in loco dicit: in qua mensura mensi fueritis, in ea remetietur uobis et qui seruus post dimissum sibi a domino omne debitum conseruo suo noluit ipse dimittere in carcerem religatur. quia indulgere conseruo noluit, quod sibi a Domino indultum fuerat amisit. quae adhuc fortius Christus in praeceptis suis maiore censurae suae uigore proponit. cum steteritis, inquit, ad orationem, remittite si quid habetis aduersus aliquem, ut et pater uester qui in caelis est remittat peccata uobis. si autem uos non remiseritis, neque pater uester qui in caelis est remittet uobis peccata uestra. excusatio tibi nulla in die iudicii superest, cum secundum tuam sententiam iudiceris et quod feceris hoc et ipse patiaris. pacificos enim et concordes adque unanimes esse in domo sua Deus praecepit et quales nos fecit secunda natiuitate tales uult renatos perseuerare, ut qui filii Dei sumus in Dei pace maneamus, et quibus spiritus unus est unus sit et animus et sensus. sic nec sacrificium Deus recipit dissidentis et ab altari reuertentem prius fratri reconciliari iubet, ut pacificis precibus et Deus possit esse pacatus. sacrificium Deo maius est pax nostra et fraterna concordia et de unitate Patris et Filii et Spiritus sancti plebs adunata.
orientation: Cyprian is explaining the petition about debts, and now presses the condition attached to it: we must forgive others if we want our own sins forgiven.
pass_a_gloss: He plainly added and attached a law binding us by a fixed condition and promise, so that we ask for our debts to be forgiven us just as we ourselves forgive our debtors, knowing that what we ask for our sins cannot be obtained unless we ourselves have done the same toward our sinners. Therefore also in another place he says: in what measure you have measured, it will be measured back to you. And the servant who, after the whole debt had been forgiven him by the lord, refused himself to forgive his fellow servant is bound in prison. Because he refused to forgive his fellow servant, he lost what had been forgiven him by the Lord. These things Christ sets forth still more strongly in his precepts with the greater force of his severity. When you stand, he says, to pray, forgive if you have anything against anyone, so that your Father who is in heaven may forgive you your sins. But if you do not forgive, neither will your Father who is in heaven forgive you your sins. No excuse remains for you on the day of judgment, since you will be judged according to your own sentence and what you have done, this you yourself will suffer. For God has commanded that the peaceful and the harmonious and the unanimous be in his house, and such as he made us by the second birth he wishes the reborn to continue to be, so that we who are children of God may remain in God's peace, and those for whom the spirit is one may also be one in mind and thought. Thus God does not receive the sacrifice of a person who is at variance, and he commands the one returning from the altar first to be reconciled to his brother, so that by peaceful prayers God also may be able to be at peace. A greater sacrifice to God is our peace and brotherly concord and a people united from the unity of the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit.

choices.why: The word denotes a formal pledge or undertaking; 'promise' keeps the binding, contractual force Cyprian stresses.
The glossary uses 'debts' for debita; keeping 'debtors' preserves the financial metaphor of sin as debt.
A literal rendering of the unusual phrase 'our sinners' keeps Cyprian's pointed reciprocity: those who sin against us.
The verb religo means to bind or tie; rendering it literally preserves the image of imprisonment as binding.

choices.english: with the greater force of his severity
choices.why: Censura here means strict judgment or severity; 'force of his severity' keeps the legal and disciplinary tone.
The word means 'of one mind'; 'unanimous' is the closest English equivalent and preserves the emphasis on shared mind and will.

pass_b_english: He went on to add a law that binds us under a fixed condition and promise: we are to ask that our debts be forgiven us just as we ourselves forgive our debtors, knowing that what we ask for our sins cannot be obtained unless we do the same toward those who sin against us. That is why he also says in another place: With the measure you use, it will be measured back to you (Matthew 7:2). And the servant who, after his master forgave him his whole debt, refused to forgive his fellow servant is bound in prison (Matthew 18:28-34). Because he would not pardon his fellow servant, he lost what the Lord had pardoned to him. Christ sets this out still more forcefully in his commands, with the greater force of his severity. When you stand to pray, he says, forgive whatever you have against anyone, so that your Father in heaven may forgive you your sins. But if you do not forgive, neither will your Father in heaven forgive you your sins (Mark 11:25; Matthew 6:15). You have no excuse left on the day of judgment, since you will be judged by your own sentence, and what you have done you will suffer yourself. For God has commanded those in his house to be peaceable, harmonious, and unanimous, and as he made us in the second birth, so he wills us to continue as reborn: we who are children of God are to remain in God's peace, and those who have one Spirit are to have one mind and one thought. So God does not receive the sacrifice of a person at odds with others, and he commands the one returning from the altar first to be reconciled to his brother, so that God may be at peace with peaceable prayers (Matthew 5:24). Our peace and brotherly concord and a people gathered into the unity of the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit are a greater sacrifice to God.

problems.quote: and so is a people gathered into one from the unity of the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit
problems.source_quote: et de unitate Patris et Filii et Spiritus sancti plebs adunata
problems.why: The people are gathered into one FROM the unity of the Trinity; English reads as a separate clause, losing that the people ARE the greater sacrifice.
problems.fix: and a people gathered into one from the unity of the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit is a greater sacrifice to God.
problems.ruling: Latin 'et de unitate...plebs adunata' is appositive/coordinate with 'sacrificium'; English 'and so is' makes it a separate clause, weakening that the gathered people ARE the sacrifice.

problems.quote: what the Lord had pardoned in him
problems.source_quote: quod sibi a Domino indultum fuerat
problems.why: 'Indultum fuerat' means 'had been granted/pardoned to him,' but 'in him' adds a wrong preposition; it was pardoned to him, not in him.
problems.fix: what the Lord had pardoned to him
problems.ruling: 'sibi...indultum fuerat' = 'had been pardoned to him'; 'in him' misrepresents the dative, changing meaning.

problems.quote: Our peace and brotherly concord are a greater sacrifice to God
problems.source_quote: sacrificium Deo maius est pax nostra et fraterna concordia
problems.why: The English omits 'et de unitate...plebs adunata' as a separate clause with its own verb; it merges it awkwardly with 'and so is'.
problems.fix: Our peace and brotherly concord are a greater sacrifice to God, and a people gathered into one from the unity of the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit.
problems.ruling: 'et de unitate...plebs adunata' is a distinct clause; 'and so is' merges it awkwardly, obscuring the people's unity reference.

edits.old: Our peace and brotherly concord are a greater sacrifice to God, and so is a people gathered into one from the unity of the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit.
edits.new: Our peace and brotherly concord are a greater sacrifice to God, and a people gathered into one from the unity of the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit is a greater sacrifice to God.

edits.old: what the Lord had pardoned in him
edits.new: what the Lord had pardoned to him

fixed: The people are indeed part of the greater sacrifice; the English now makes the people a second subject of 'are a greater sacrifice to God' rather than a separate clause.
The source 'indultum fuerat' means 'had been granted/pardoned to him,' not 'in him'; corrected to 'to him'.

problems.quote: a people gathered into one from the unity of the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit is a greater sacrifice to God
problems.source_quote: de unitate Patris et Filii et Spiritus sancti plebs adunata
problems.why: 'De unitate' means 'out of/from the unity' but the syntax suggests 'a people gathered into the unity of' or 'in unity with.' The English 'from' misrepresents the theological claim.
problems.fix: a people gathered into the unity of the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit is a greater sacrifice to God

problems.quote: Our peace and brotherly concord are a greater sacrifice to God, and a people gathered into one from the unity of the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit is a greater sacrifice to God
problems.source_quote: sacrificium Deo maius est pax nostra et fraterna concordia et de unitate Patris et Filii et Spiritus sancti plebs adunata
problems.why: The English adds 'is a greater sacrifice to God' twice, making two separate claims. The Latin has one predicate 'sacrificium Deo maius est' for two subjects joined by 'et.'
problems.fix: Our peace and brotherly concord and a people gathered into the unity of the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit are a greater sacrifice to God
problems.ruling: Latin has one predicate 'sacrificium Deo maius est' for two subjects; English duplicates it, distorting sentence structure.

edits.old: Our peace and brotherly concord are a greater sacrifice to God, and a people gathered into one from the unity of the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit is a greater sacrifice to God.
edits.new: Our peace and brotherly concord and a people gathered into the unity of the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit are a greater sacrifice to God.

fixed: Merged the two predicates into one, matching the single predicate 'sacrificium Deo maius est' with two subjects joined by 'et'; changed 'from the unity' to 'into the unity' to reflect 'de unitate' as the source of the gathering.

last_rejected.why: Latin 'sponaione' means 'pledge/guarantee', not 'promise' in the sense of a reward offered.
last_rejected.ruling: 'Promise' is within normal range for 'sponsio' (solemn engagement/pledge); no meaning changed.

last_rejected.quote: With the measure you use, it will be measured back to you (Matthew 7:2)
last_rejected.source_quote: in qua mensura mensi fueritis, in ea remetietur uobis
last_rejected.why: The source does not attribute this to Matthew 7:2; Cyprian presents it as a general saying of Christ without specifying a text.
last_rejected.fix: With the measure you use, it will be measured back to you.
last_rejected.ruling: Source 'in alio loco dicit' implies a scripture reference; Matthew 7:2 is standard editorial identification, not misleading.

last_rejected.quote: And the servant who, after his master forgave him his whole debt, refused to forgive his fellow servant is bound in prison (Matthew 18:28-34)
last_rejected.source_quote: qui seruus post dimissum sibi a domino omne debitum conseruo suo noluit ipse dimittere in carcerem religatur
last_rejected.why: The source does not cite Matthew 18:28-34; Cyprian presents this as a narrative illustration without scriptural attribution.
last_rejected.fix: And the servant who, after his master forgave him his whole debt, refused to forgive his fellow servant is bound in prison.
last_rejected.ruling: Source 'in alio loco dicit' introduces scripture; Matthew 18:28-34 is standard editorial identification of the parable, not misleading.

last_rejected.quote: When you stand to pray, he says, forgive whatever you have against anyone, so that your Father in heaven may forgive you your sins. But if you do not forgive, neither will your Father in heaven forgive you your sins (Mark 11:25; Matthew 6:15)
last_rejected.source_quote: cum steteritis, inquit, ad orationem, remittite si quid habetis aduersus aliquem, ut et pater uester qui in caelis est remittat peccata uobis. si autem uos non remiseritis, neque pater uester qui in caelis est remittet uobis peccata uestra
last_rejected.why: The source attributes this quotation to Christ with 'inquit' but does not cite Mark 11:25 or Matthew 6:15; these are editorial additions.
last_rejected.fix: When you stand to pray, he says, forgive whatever you have against anyone, so that your Father in heaven may forgive you your sins. But if you do not forgive, neither will your Father in heaven forgive you your sins.
last_rejected.ruling: Source 'inquit' attributes words to Christ; Mark 11:25 and Matthew 6:15 are standard editorial identifications, not misleading.

last_rejected.quote: so that God may be at peace with peaceable prayers (Matthew 5:24)
last_rejected.source_quote: ut pacificis precibus et Deus possit esse pacatus
last_rejected.why: The source does not cite Matthew 5:24; this is an editorial addition not in the Latin text.
last_rejected.fix: so that God may be at peace with peaceable prayers.
last_rejected.ruling: Matthew 5:24 is standard editorial reference for altar/reconciliation teaching; not misleading to reader.

last_rejected.why: The English adds 'he says' before the quotation, but 'inquit' in the source refers back to Christ from earlier in the paragraph, not introducing a new speaker here.
last_rejected.fix: When you stand to pray, forgive whatever you have against anyone...
last_rejected.ruling: 'inquit' means 'he says'; English renders it correctly. Claim that it refers back is not a translation error.

last_rejected.quote: with the greater force of his severity
last_rejected.why: 'censura' means judgment/authority/discipline, not 'severity'; 'vigor' means force/vigor, and the phrase means 'with greater vigor of his judgment/authority'.
last_rejected.fix: with greater vigor of his authority
last_rejected.ruling: 'censura' includes 'severity' within its range; rendering is acceptable, not a changed meaning.

last_rejected.quote: a people gathered into the unity of the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit
last_rejected.source_quote: de unitate Patris et Filii et Spiritus sancti plebs adunata
last_rejected.why: de unitate marks the Trinity's unity as the source of the people's oneness, not a unity they are gathered into.
last_rejected.fix: a people made one from the unity of the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit
last_rejected.ruling: "de unitate Patris et Filii et Spiritus sancti plebs adunata" is Cyprian's famous phrase; "a people gathered from/into the unity of the Trinity" are both acceptable, and the English conveys the sense without changing meaning.
